narr: A warm front was present across the Deep South moving towards the Tennessee Valley throughout the day, with WPC analyzing a secondary stationary boundary developing along the Ohio River by the evening. Overall forcing was not strong across the state of Kentucky, however. Most of the state remained dry throughout the day, however a few isolated showers and thunderstorms developed across the far southeast part of the state into the evening. The storm across Bell county was the strongest, and with very little flow aloft, the storm did not move much. It continued to sit over the county for a couple of hours, eventually leading to a handful of flash flooding reports. In addition, winds from the storm led to trees being downed onto KY-119 near the community of Miracle.
